hook_text: Same molecule. Same reagent. Two completely different products. The whole secret is printed on the label.
clip_script: Here is the best-kept secret in organic chemistry: molecules do not choose their reactions — conditions do. Watch this. Take 2-bromopentane and sodium hydroxide. Serve the hydroxide dilute, in water, gently warmed, and you get a polite exchange: the hydroxide taps the bromine on the shoulder and takes its exact seat on the chain. Substitution — out comes an alcohol. Now the SAME two chemicals, but the hydroxide concentrated, dissolved in ethanol, at a rolling boil — and the mood flips completely. A hydrogen gets ripped off the neighbouring carbon, the bromine storms out the other side, and a double bond snaps shut across the gap. Elimination — out comes an alkene. Same partners, different lighting, different dance. And that double bond? Think of it as a pair of open hands. Alkenes grab whatever you offer: hydrogen with a nickel catalyst turns runny oil into margarine; bromine loses its red-brown colour the moment those hands close — the classic alkene test. When the offer has two different pieces, remember the gossip rule: the rich get richer — the new hydrogen joins the carbon that already owns more hydrogens. So read every reaction question in this order: conditions first, molecule second, answer almost automatic. Hot concentrated acid means a double bond is coming. Light on an alkane means a swap. The question prints the conditions because the conditions ARE the answer.
visual_style: A dance floor where the same two molecule characters change routines as the lighting shifts from cool blue to blazing red; a double bond drawn as open hands snatching bromine and draining its colour; condition words stamped across the screen like passwords.
mood: Insider-tip energy — the cheat code to a feared topic, handed over.
pacing: One-two reveal of the same reagents giving two products, quick open-hands montage, punchy conditions-first close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and let the conditions answer the questions for you.
